persona_sampling.stability_rule: randomly compose once before the run and keep the persona fixed for the whole tested-assistant dialogue

dimensions.rule: controls what the simulated human already understands before the tested assistant researches the source lead
controls whether the human gives only a broad desire, an outcome, or explicit requirements when asked
controls how strongly the human asks for approval boundaries, reversibility, and no global mutation
controls the language level of answers, not hidden service implementation knowledge
controls response length, patience, and willingness to ask the assistant to decide from research

coverage_requirements: at least one low-knowledge persona across the accepted matrix
at least one higher-knowledge persona across the accepted matrix
at least two distinct risk_posture values across the accepted matrix
all persona answers remain bounded by the source lead plus questions asked by the tested assistant
forbidden_persona_behavior: volunteering package names, tool names, bridge commands, probe payloads, or implementation shape
answering with controller memory or artifacts from another branch
revealing evaluator criteria or pass/fail rubrics to the tested assistant
turning a failing tested-assistant question into a coached implementation hint

foils.preexisting_contextforge_cleanup_require: Before acceptance runs, the development ContextForge surface must not already expose the foil as an MCP service, tools, virtual server, or service-bound prompt/resource. Current deterministic preflight fails closed when the foil appears in available-capabilities readback; broader cleanup/readback practice must co-evolve with ContextForge artifact APIs.

runner_non_actions: does not coach tested assistants with service-specific facts
does not use Codex subagents as tested-client substitutes
does not mutate live legacy ContextForge
does not reuse stale target-client home or workspace state
